title: QUIC RFC 9000 S9P6P1 Preferred Address Validation Failure Policy
purpose: Describe the focused S9P6P1 closure for keeping the original server address authoritative after preferred-address validation fails.
design_summary: A failed preferred-address validation marks that preferred-address candidate abandoned without promoting it and without discarding the connection while the original server address remains the active path. Future non-probing sends continue to use the original server address.
data_and_state_considerations: Path-validation failure still abandons the failed candidate and clears its validation deadline. When the failed candidate is a non-active preferred-address path, the active original path is preserved even if no path has separately been marked validated. This keeps the connection alive on the original server address while preventing the failed preferred path from becoming a recently validated or active path.
edge_cases_and_constraints: IPv4 preferred-address validation failure keeps future sends on the original IPv4 server address.
IPv6 preferred-address validation failure keeps future sends on the original IPv6 server address.
The failed preferred-address candidate remains abandoned and is not promoted.
The preferred-address path is not added to the recently validated path cache after failure.
risks: This slice does not add preferred-address retry policy after validation failure.
This slice does not prove server preferred_address emission.
This slice does not close deferred fuzz obligations for S9P6P1.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S9P6P1-0005 only. It does not claim complete S9P6P1 closure, preferred_address transport-parameter emission proof, per-family metadata cleanup, public migration APIs, multipath support, hosted interop readiness, or closure of deferred fuzz obligations.
